newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss summer 1996 hotel stays lowest since 1959.
newsitem.headline: Swiss summer 1996 hotel stays lowest since 1959.

text.p: Overnight stays in Swiss hotels fell 5.2 percent in the summer half-year to the lowest level since 1959, the Federal Statistics Office said on Monday, blaming the weak economy, bad weather and a strong Swiss franc.

Its survey of Swiss hotels showed 16.8 million stays in the May-October period, 923,000 fewer than in the same period of 1995, when stays had fallen 5.6 percent. The latest decline marked the six consecutive drop in the measure.

Guest-night stays by Swiss visitors dropped four percent to 6.83 million and the average length of stay slipped to 2.4 nights from 2.5, it said, citing Switzerland's stagnant economy and poor weather.

Foreigners' stays fell six percent to 9.97 million guest-nights. "The uncertain economic situation in individual source countries as well as unfavourable exchange-rate conditions may have been decisive for the negative result."

Swiss remained atop the list of visitors with 40 percent of guest-nights, followed by visitors from Germany (18.9 percent), the United States (6.8 percent), Britain (4.2 percent), Japan (4.0 percent) and France (3.4 percent).
